summary.text: A 54-year-old male attended the clinic with infiltrative solid-type basal cell carcinoma of the right nasal ala, confirmed as malignant. The same site had been treated six months earlier with resection and a paramedian forehead flap, with positive margins. History included tobacco and alcohol use, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and HIV with undetectable viral load. The lesion, approximately 10x15 mm, was pearly and ulcerated with telangiectasias, clinically highly suggestive of nodular-ulcerative basal cell carcinoma.

The right nasal ala and vestibule were resected and the defect was covered with a paramedian forehead flap with a vertical pedicle about 2 cm wide, the contralateral side being unavailable because the supratrochlear artery was sacrificed in the prior procedure. A full-thickness skin graft was fashioned into a tubular structure, sutured to the nasal vestibule mucosa as mucosal lining, and the flap was opened to let it cover the new nostril. Cotton in a glove finger supported the nostril; cartilage harvest was not required.

After flap elevation he was hospitalized with daily wound care for seven days while the flap showed adequate vascularization. Anterior rhinoscopy and the NOSE scale were used to assess airway patency, with a score of 45 points indicating moderate obstruction attributed to postoperative edema. A photograph seven days after surgery showed a viable flap. He was discharged home, and the authors describe a favorable early course with satisfactory structural support.
